frozen_claim.title: Colorado/Denver local-entity neuron with narrow unanchored-identifier suppression
frozen_claim.lede: The positive pole is driven by explicit Colorado, Denver, or Boulder entities and the local contexts they license—addresses, phone numbers, citations, datelines, state-history enumerations, and nearby spaces, punctuation, or numbers. It also fires for unambiguously Colorado local institutions and landmarks even without the word Colorado. The negative pole is sparse: mostly unanchored dense identifier blocks and one other-state “Natural Heritage” label; broad non-Colorado geography is not supported. Many no-visible-cue cases remain unresolved.
frozen_claim.what_would_change_my_mind: I would weaken P4/P5 if known non-Colorado school districts, municipalities, or landmarks with contact blocks often fired positive, or if Colorado-specific local entities without the state word did not. I would revise N2 if dense unanchored identifiers were frequently positive outside a recognized Colorado frame, or if recognized Colorado local institutional frames still produced negative identifier blocks. I would drop N3 if other-state “Natural Heritage” labels were consistently positive. I would broaden the negative pole only if other-state administrative, legal, geographic, or natural contexts reliably and strongly predicted negative responses without Colorado cues; the measured positives among non-Colorado contexts count against that. Unexplained strong responses such as “in Bolivia” or other local-place passages remain unresolved unless a recurring contextual pattern appears.
frozen_claim.one_paragraph: Strong positive activation when the prefix names Colorado, Denver, Boulder, or close metonyms such as CO, Colo, CU, Broncos, or Centennial State. The marked token is often a nearby space, punctuation mark, “at”, “is”, or following numeral, but the preceding context contains the place/entity. Exact place tokens are strongest; weaker toponyms need an explicit Colorado frame. Generic place strings, non-Colorado states, and purely geological “Colorado Plateaus” uses without a state/entity frame do not reliably fire. Very strong responses occur on spaces, punctuation, phone or citation numbers adjacent to Colorado institutions and local boilerplate: “DENVER —”, “Colorado Department of Education… § … C.R.S.”, “University of Colorado… 720…”, “Colorado State University Extension… colostate.edu”, “9NEWS”, “Colorado Women’s Education Foundation”. The Colorado entity must be present in the prefix; a bare phone, address, or statute string is not sufficient. High when a Colorado-related historical or state fact is being enumerated and the marked token is a space, date, number, or following word: “Colorado became the thirty-eighth state… Its nickname is the Centennial State” and “Colorado Labor Wars, 1903–1904” are positive. The pattern needs the Colorado frame; bare dates, numbers, or historical lists in other states are weak or negative. Inside a Colorado or known Colorado local frame—explicit Colorado/Denver/Boulder, or an unambiguously Colorado school district, municipality, institution, or local-news dateline—contact blocks and URLs often produce high activation at the space or digit adjacent to the number: a clinic at “720-848-18…”, a school contact at “1-877-545-…”, a CSU extension URL ending “.html”, and the local-media marker “9NEWS”. The local Colorado frame must be in the prefix; a bare 720/303 number or generic contact block is not enough. Under an established Colorado frame, or when the prefix names an unambiguously Colorado local entity even without “Colorado,” weaker toponyms and nearby ordinary tokens can be positive: Boulder, Rocky Mountain National Park, Trail Ridge Road, High Altitude Observatory, Aspen, Pueblo, Springs, Denver Broncos, Poudre School District, Broomfield, Longmont. The same word in another state, generic geology, or a broad western topic does not fire; use only with local Colorado support or an unambiguous Colorado entity.
frozen_claim.negative_pole: Strong negative at the central punctuation/digit of dense identifier strings—telephone groups with parentheses or hyphens, ZIP/address fragments, statute/legal citations of the “§ 28-33-02” type, grant IDs, and long comma-grouped area or statistical figures—when the prefix lacks any Colorado/Denver/Boulder frame or an unambiguously Colorado local entity such as Poudre School District, Broomfield, High Altitude Observatory, or Trail Ridge Road. The sign attaches to the whole formatted block, often at a space, comma, hyphen, parenthesis, or single digit. Ordinary dates, small counts, email-only contact labels, geographically nonspecific numbers, and any contact/citation inside a recognized Colorado local institutional frame are weak, unreliable, or positive under P2/P4. Negative for the capitalized label or adjacent token in an other-state natural-heritage program name such as “Alaska Natural Heritage Program” when it is outside a Colorado frame. This does not generalize to nature, wildlife, parks, outdoor recreation, rivers, mountains, or other-state geography: many such non-Colorado natural and geographical passages are positive or neutral. The cue is the program-label construction, not the topic of natural heritage.

input_excerpt.focus: State what the neuron primarily responds to and the conditions for strong activation. Focus on the strongest supported pattern. Use matched controls and counterexamples to bound it. Leave the negative pole and proposed tests to their own paragraphs.

section_summaries.spectrum: The measured spectrum is heavy near zero but strongly right-skewed: the corpus median is −0.048 with p99.99 = 91.0 and maximum 306.0 against minimum −44.5, while the equal-quota bins place most N2 cases in negative bins and most P1/P2 cases in upper positive bins, with no-visible-cue cases spread across the range. Clear counterexamples remain: a scored space before an unanchored Qinghai area figure is −44.5, a scored space before a Colorado statutory citation is 306.0, and unrelated “rich” and “Io” tokens are near zero. The key qualification is that these bins are quota-sampled rather than population frequencies, many no-visible-cue and some extreme cases remain unresolved, and the pattern is observational unless supported by measured ablations and same-position controls rather than treated as a demonstrated causal route.
section_summaries.search: In the search section, L55_N11703 produced strong positive scores when the causal prefix named Colorado/Denver/Boulder or an unambiguous Colorado local institution and the scored token was an adjacent space or ordinary token (320 at “University of Colorado Health scheduling desk: ”, 320 at “Poudre School District contact: ”, 241 at “ is”, 225 at “ near”). The main qualification is that these are prefix-conditioned scores at the marked position: the negative search cases score the dense identifier or label token itself (-44.25 at the Elko, NV identifier block; -40.0 at “Natural”), and the frozen explanation explicitly says bare phone/address/citation strings without a Colorado frame are not sufficient. Those negatives preserve the stated counterexamples to a broad non-Colorado-geography negative pole, but the supplied search cases do not by themselves establish broader route predictions.
section_summaries.custom: In the custom controlled sweeps, the positive pole is context-gated: a Colorado dateline (“Centennial State”) reaches 146.0 versus 1.04 for Portland, and a CU Health contact block reaches 320.0 while otherwise identical Nevada and Bismarck Department of Agriculture blocks are negative (−20.9 and −30.0). The key qualification is that dense-identifier negativity is form- and frame-dependent rather than a general number effect: the full Elko identifier block is strongly negative (−39.75), but its long area figure alone is near neutral/positive (0.98) and a small count is near neutral (−0.27), while Colorado Natural Heritage is strongly positive (158.0) and the negative Alaska Fish and Game label (−23.4) does not transfer to Sierra Nevada (−0.76). These are measured controlled-sweep observations; the broader Colorado-local-entity and narrow unanchored-identifier account remains a medium-confidence hypothesis, with unresolved cases noted in the frozen explanation.
section_summaries.tests: On the saved 11-case test split, route prediction was 72.7% accurate (8/11) against an 18.2% baseline, with the confusion concentrated in n2 postal/address-to-phone cases predicted as n1 and one p1 Colorado public-affairs case predicted as p3. The blind maximum and minimum were directionally consistent with the frozen explanation but weaker than the targets: 282 versus 306 at the Colorado clinic/contact space, and -25.75 versus -44.5 at the Alaska Natural Heritage token. These are small saved-split and blind-case results, so they support the frozen route/pole account only within the measured tests and do not establish broader generalization.
section_summaries.criticism: N2 remains a narrowed, context-dependent suppression rather than a general non-Colorado suppressor: dense non-Colorado identifiers are usually negative (Elko Basque Club 775 strongly negative), and the author-initial block is near zero, but a genuine Utah clinic phone block with 801 is positive (+4.78) and a Colorado area code inside a contact block can flip even Elko community center 720 to +180 while Nevada Department of Agriculture with 720 stays negative. Local entity alone is insufficient; the sign depends on the interaction of area code, contact block, and institutional label. P4/P5 hold only in a narrowed form: Colorado-named/local entities are strongly positive and natural non-Colorado named local entities are mostly weak/negative, but positivity is not entity-specific. A generic 'Scheduling desk: 720-' block reaches +193 versus near-zero 212, and Elko community center flips from -6.97 with 212 to +180 with 720, while Nevada Department of Agriculture stays negative with 720 (-20.9). Natural non-Colorado contact blocks were mostly untested because Round 1 anchors were entity names, and the one King County phone-adjacent case was weak/negative, so the contact-block-specific claim remains limited. N3 is narrowed to a label-token effect: Alaska Natural Heritage and Alaska Fish & Game/Natural Resources labels are strongly negative, while Colorado Natural Heritage, Rocky Mountain National Park, and Trail Ridge Road controls are positive; NH/ND agency-label tokens also lean negative, but the NH whole label is mixed and the ND passage is confounded by a 701 phone block. The reliable cue is other-state program/agency label tokens outside a Colorado frame, not broad nature, parks, or whole-passage suppression. The strong no-cue cases are not captured by a single local-place/document rule: all five have near-anchor local-place/admin/numeric framing, but that feature appears in both positive cases (La Paz +157, CU Boulder +256, 720 manual +150) and negative cases (Qinghai -43.75, Springdale -37.5). The local-news/dateline genre hypothesis is rejected because positive no-cue cases include a research article and a parenting manual, while controlled Denver/Colorado datelines are positive but Boise is only weakly positive; causal-prefix confounds remain. Thus unresolved heterogeneity is supported, but no sign-tracking cue was identified.

spectrum.sampling: Equal quotas across nonempty activation bins, with positions spread deterministically across each full-corpus bin. Bins below quota contribute all their positions; the shortfall is shared across other bins.

output.text: The strongest supported pattern is a prefix-gated Colorado local-entity response: L55_N11703 fires most strongly when the causal prefix explicitly names Colorado, Denver, Boulder, or close metonyms, or an unambiguously Colorado local institution or landmark, and the scored token is a nearby space, punctuation mark, ordinary token, or contact-adjacent digit. Matched controlled sweeps support this as context-gated rather than a generic place or number effect—Colorado dateline and CU Health contact frames are strongly positive while otherwise identical Nevada and Bismarck blocks are not—and counterexamples show that bare phone, address, or citation strings, generic non-Colorado toponyms, and purely geological “Colorado Plateaus” uses without a state or entity frame do not reliably fire. The account remains a medium-confidence hypothesis: local entity alone is insufficient, with the sign depending on the interaction of area code, contact block, and institutional label, and unresolved no-cue cases keep the boundary uncertain.
